title: Sunrise service
hookLine: Protestants often gather outdoors at dawn on Easter morning

lines: CHAIRS ON WET GRASS, FACING EAST.
cards: Folding chairs on wet grass, set out in rows facing east. A hillside, a park, a beach, a churchyard. It's cold and still mostly dark, and people arrive in coats with blankets and thermoses, talking in low voices.
A guitar is tuned somewhere, or a little brass band warms up. Nobody has lit a candle. They're waiting for the sun.
Then, as the sky over the hill goes from gray to pink, they start to sing. Some Protestant churches gather like this on Easter morning, outdoors, timed to the dawn.

teach.h: AT THE RISING OF THE SUN.
teach.b: Why dawn? Because that's when the Gospels say the women went to the tomb, and they don't all describe the light the same way.
Mark, in the King James, says they came "very early in the morning the first day of the week" and "at the rising of the sun."

teach.h: EARLY, WHEN IT WAS YET DARK.
teach.b: John says Mary Magdalene came "early, when it was yet dark." One has the sun coming up, the other still dark. A sunrise service sits right in that half-light.
Stay with John's version. Mary finds the stone rolled away and the tomb empty. She stands outside weeping.

A man speaks to her, and she takes him for the gardener and asks where they've put the body. Then, in the King James: "Jesus saith unto her, Mary. She turned herself, and saith unto him, Rabboni; which is to say, Master."
She doesn't know him by his face.

teach.h: SHE KNOWS HIM WHEN HE SAYS HER NAME.
teach.b: She knows him when he says her name.
Tradition traces the outdoor dawn service to Moravian Christians, and some Moravian congregations still gather in their graveyards at sunrise on Easter, among the graves, to sing.

Other churches gather on hillsides, in parks, on beaches. The setting changes; the hour doesn't. People get up in the cold and stand in the dark on purpose, the way the women did, and wait for it to get light.

how: Some Protestant congregations hold an Easter sunrise service outdoors, on a hill, in a park or churchyard, with hymns and the Gospel reading of the empty tomb as the sun comes up; some Moravian congregations hold theirs in their burial grounds.

games.q: you're Mary Magdalene, weeping outside the empty tomb. a man you take for the gardener asks why you're crying. what happens next?
o: he explains the scriptures to you.
he says your name, and you know him.
he walks away without a word.
games.why: "Jesus saith unto her, Mary." she turns and says, Rabboni. it's her name that does it.

practice: If it's dawn, go to a window facing the light; if not, turn toward the brightest window or lamp nearby, or close your eyes and remember a sunrise you've seen.
Notice how slowly the light comes, gray first, then color; nothing about it hurries. If you pray, sit in the quiet the way Mary stood at the tomb, listening; if not, simply watch.

wordCard.voice: Sunrise service. An Easter service held outdoors at dawn, at the hour the Gospels say the women came to the tomb.

orig.note: Mary's word to Jesus in John 20:16; John explains it means master.
